sources.title: Study guide for Exam AI-200: Developing AI Cloud Solutions on Azure
sources.shortSummary: Fresh MCP retrieval confirms the unchanged undated four-domain, nine-skill, 27-subskill AI-200 outline and its stated weights. The original undated content identity is retained; this retrieval does not establish exam GA status or implementation behavior.

sources.title: Define ConfigMaps for application settings
sources.shortSummary: configMapKeyRef/envFrom and file-volume consumption; ordinary mounted files refresh, environment values need restart and subPath does not auto-refresh. Application reload behavior is supplied explicitly in stems.

sources.title: Implement secrets for sensitive data
sources.shortSummary: secretKeyRef injection and describe secret metadata/key inspection without secret values. CSI/App Configuration product links are not used without fresh separate supporting retrieval.

sources.title: Create Kubernetes deployment manifests
sources.shortSummary: Deployment replicas, image references and matching template labels; CPU/memory requests guide scheduling. Excludes recommended fixed production replica counts and false equivalence of CPU/memory limit behavior.

sources.title: Expose applications in Azure Kubernetes Services
sources.shortSummary: Service selectors, client port versus targetPort and documented ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer/ExternalName purposes. Public LoadBalancer examples are not universal claims about internal load balancers.

sources.title: Deploy applications to Azure Kubernetes Services
sources.shortSummary: kubectl apply submits desired state asynchronously; inspect readiness and actual application requests; previous-container logs and scheduling event inspection. No automatic ACR authorization assumption.

sources.title: Deploy containers to Azure App Service
sources.shortSummary: Linux App Service image selection and explicit registry authentication; changing image tags and same-tag push pickup via restart or configured registry webhook. No ARM-audience requirement is inferred from this unit.

sources.title: Configure container runtime behavior
sources.shortSummary: Conventional Linux custom-container CMD override, WEBSITES_PORT routing, and enabled /home storage across restart and scale-out. Excludes sidecar behavior and broad health-check timing guarantees.

sources.title: Configure application settings
sources.shortSummary: Runtime app settings, typed connection-string prefixes, and Key Vault reference prerequisites and resolution. Slot stickiness is documented but not used to recreate the known cross-bank duplicate.

sources.title: Observe and troubleshoot containerized apps
sources.shortSummary: Container stdout/stderr logs, SCM Environment and mounted-file views, and distinction between SCM and the actual application container. SSH requires image support; no secret values should be displayed.

sources.title: Explore Container Apps environments
sources.shortSummary: Environment networking/logging/lifecycle boundaries and internal versus external ingress. Optional CLI preview extension flag is not used or treated as ordinary baseline functionality.

sources.title: Deploy a container app using the Azure CLI and YAML
sources.shortSummary: CLI create/update flows, image changes creating revisions and YAML as the configuration source overriding other configuration flags. Application/resource selectors remain necessary.

sources.title: Configure runtime settings with environment variables and secrets
sources.shortSummary: Nonsensitive environment values versus CLI secretref and template secretRef; externalized secret values and template configuration. No invented Key Vault CLI syntax is used.

sources.title: Configure image pull authentication for private registries
sources.shortSummary: Registry authentication is separate from application configuration. An assigned identity with registry pull permission must be selected in registry configuration; username/password remains an alternative for suitable registries.

sources.title: Verify deployments with logs and status
sources.shortSummary: Console versus system logs and app/revision/replica inspection during deployment verification. Successful image provisioning alone is not application health.

sources.title: Update images and manage revisions safely
sources.shortSummary: Image updates, per-revision configuration comparison and deactivation preserving investigation evidence. No unsupported revision deletion command or retention guarantee is authored.

sources.title: Monitor logs and troubleshoot issues
sources.shortSummary: Revision-specific failure isolation by console logs and configuration comparison; safe correlation/build metadata without raw sensitive prompts.

sources.title: Configure health probes and troubleshoot failures
sources.shortSummary: Readiness gates request routing while liveness failure restarts replicas. Probe paths and initial delays should match measured application behavior; YAML patterns are not treated as executable deployment validation.

sources.title: Monitor application logs and metrics
sources.shortSummary: Explicit namespace and container selection for logs; metrics-server prerequisite for kubectl top; combine utilization with application and event evidence.

sources.title: Troubleshoot pods and services
sources.shortSummary: Pod events distinguish pull, startup and scheduling failures; Service selector/targetPort/EndpointSlice checks; permanent repairs belong in manifests rather than container shells.

sources.title: Verify service connectivity and endpoints
sources.shortSummary: Service-to-Pod endpoint inspection, local port-forward testing and separate verification of public load-balancer/ingress paths. A successful local tunnel is not proof of external connectivity.

sources.title: Configure scale rules
sources.shortSummary: Scale limits, HTTP/TCP/resource triggers and independent rule signals. Excludes disputed HTTP averaging, generalized billing and unsupported precise scale-step assertions.

sources.title: Implement event-driven scaling with KEDA
sources.shortSummary: Service Bus queue versus subscription metadata, backlog threshold, supported authentication mappings, and Event Hubs consumer-group partition/lag limits. Excludes the unit’s inconsistent message-throughput example.

sources.title: Apply KEDA scalers for custom workloads
sources.shortSummary: Cron active-window baseline combined with reactive rules selects the highest requested count; ScaledObject-to-Container Apps mapping. Non-Learn KEDA links are not source approvals; Kafka parameter examples are not used.

sources.title: Choose and apply revision modes
sources.shortSummary: Template versus application changes; ready single-mode handoff; multiple-mode traffic and ordinary revision labels; independent per-revision replica minima. No preview deployment-label mode, retention limit or release-status inference.

sources.title: Registries, repositories, and artifacts
sources.shortSummary: Registry/repository/artifact roles; mutable tags, the omitted latest tag, manifests and shared content-addressed layers. Excludes namespace authorization claims and tier-specific capabilities.

sources.title: Build and run images with ACR Tasks
sources.shortSummary: Cloud quick builds, local/Git/tarball context selection, task triggers and run operations, .dockerignore upload reduction and Dockerfile layer caching. Excludes broad public-registry base-trigger compatibility and the erroneous throughput arithmetic example elsewhere.

sources.title: Tag and version images
sources.shortSummary: Stable release-line servicing versus never-reused build references; build and commit metadata; deployed-tag write-enabled command. No claim that write-enabled alone controls deletion, retention exemptions, purge age behavior or feature release status.

sources.title: Implement the Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL SDK
sources.shortSummary: Connects through the root CosmosClient; recommends application-lifetime client reuse, distinguishes lightweight database/container handles, point reads and queries, and create/upsert/replace item operations. Do not use the illustrative if_match snippet or expand account-key security assertions.

sources.title: Query Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL
sources.shortSummary: Documents separate name/value query parameters, partition routing, projection, page size and lazy iteration, array queries, and request-charge observation. No latency or RU number is guaranteed.

sources.title: Store and retrieve embeddings in Azure Cosmos DB
sources.shortSummary: Documents array-valued embeddings; immutable path/type/dimension/metric policies at container creation; float32, float16, int8 and uint8; vector-index types and minimum effective index population. Preserves corrected float16 support but excludes universal negligible-loss or whole-database 50-percent savings claims. Cosine scoring inconsistencies are excluded.

sources.title: Execute vector similarity queries for semantic search
sources.shortSummary: Documents VectorDistance query shape, TOP, projection, same-model query embeddings, and explicit brute-force option. The prose cosine-similarity direction conflicts with default ascending examples; no candidate relies on that scoring interpretation.

sources.title: Combine vector similarity results with metadata filtering
sources.shortSummary: Combines metadata eligibility with vector queries and explicitly targets the partition key. Optimizer-dependent pre/post filtering is not a universal exhaustive-recall or exact result-count guarantee. Hybrid full-text/RRF implementation is not used in this batch.

sources.title: Use the change feed to trigger embedding refresh
sources.shortSummary: Explains lease checkpoint/ownership/failover, push versus scheduled pull processing, selective content-hash-based refresh, and updating the embedding and content hash together. Excludes exactly-once wording, illustrative always-true refresh code, unsupported standalone runtime tables, and malformed pull start flags.

sources.title: Configure range and composite indexes
sources.shortSummary: Documents property order and full-direction reversal for composite ORDER BY, equality-first/range-last composite filtering, per-write index costs, and asynchronous add-before-remove index transformation. No nested-path specificity rule is inferred beyond the actual examples.

sources.title: Tune vector indexes for embedding workloads
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes exact flat, quantizedFlat and diskANN; 505-dimensional flat limit, 1000-vector effective-index threshold, separation from range indexing, and immutable vector policies. Optional tuning feature-release assertions and generalized prefilter guarantees are excluded.

sources.title: Reduce RU costs with strategic indexing
sources.shortSummary: Relates write costs to indexed paths and actual filter/sort workloads; compares retrieved/output metrics, selective indexing, and asynchronous transformations. Benchmark results must be interpreted for measured data rather than universal cost promises.

sources.title: Choose consistency levels for optimal performance
sources.shortSummary: Documents partition-bound session tokens and explicit handoff between SDK clients, read-your-writes versus weaker consistency, and relative read RU costs. Does not license strengthening an account default per request or promise instant ANN indexing.

sources.title: Connect to PostgreSQL
sources.shortSummary: Documents issued Entra token strings as database passwords, PostgreSQL token resource, native authentication, TLS verification modes, and direct 5432 versus enabled General Purpose/Memory Optimized PgBouncer 6432 endpoints. No username-format generalization is used.

sources.title: Create and manage schemas
sources.shortSummary: Documents typed columns, JSONB, BYTEA, NOT NULL/UNIQUE/foreign keys, composite keys, and table/index separation. Excludes the incorrect claim that RESTRICT is the default referential action and absolute trailing-index-column limitations.

sources.title: Query data
sources.shortSummary: Documents JSONB extraction and containment, keyset pagination with a unique tie-breaker, RETURNING, and ON CONFLICT. The broad SELECT alias statement about GROUP BY/LIMIT is excluded.

sources.title: Integrate SDKs and applications
sources.shortSummary: Documents psycopg parameter tuples, result-fetch modes, connection/cursor context managers, connection and statement timeouts, transient versus syntax/constraint failures, COPY batching, and application pool checkout. External library sites are not admitted sources.

sources.title: Store and query embeddings with pgvector
sources.shortSummary: Documents installed vector extension, dimensioned vector columns, dense/half/sparse representations and distinct distance operators. No omitted extension allowlisting prerequisite or model-specific output guarantee is inferred.

sources.title: Perform fast vector similarity search
sources.shortSummary: Documents IVFFlat data-dependent clustering versus HNSW empty-table construction, runtime probes/search width, and metric/operator-class correspondence. Directly links the exact pgvector performance product article. Excludes universal latency/recall targets.

sources.title: Manage index lifecycle and embedding updates
sources.shortSummary: Documents index progress/usage monitoring, deferred stale-embedding refresh, parallel model columns, table/index sizing and MVCC old row versions. Excludes the invalid 3072-dimensional standard-vector HNSW example, erroneous migration-time arithmetic, and fixed index-size multipliers.

sources.title: Run vector similarity search for semantic retrieval
sources.shortSummary: Documents metadata/index cost-based plan selection, evaluated distance thresholds plus count limits, content projections, multi-aspect and hybrid retrieval. Never assumes every ANN query physically prefilters or that a global threshold fits all corpora.

sources.title: Implement retrieval patterns for RAG pipelines
sources.shortSummary: Documents source/chunk tables, adjacency, token budgets, provenance projections, version filters, and precision/recall evaluation. No flawed DISTINCT/window snippet is reused; citation usefulness does not establish probabilistic confidence.

sources.title: Tune PostgreSQL for pgvector
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes shared_buffers, per-operation work_mem and nonallocating effective_cache_size; documents measured plans, CPU/memory/I/O and runtime search settings. Explicitly excludes the incorrect quadratic vector-distance dimension-scaling claim and integer-dividing cache-hit snippet.

sources.title: Choose and configure vector indexes
sources.shortSummary: Documents construction versus query parameters, empirical IVFFlat/HNSW tradeoffs and concurrent maintenance. Excludes universal timing, guaranteed recall and questionable dimensional/memory multipliers.

sources.title: Optimize data layout
sources.shortSummary: Documents metadata B-tree/GIN/expression indexes, partial indexes, typed-plus-flexible schemas, cost-based filtering and partition-aligned scans. Excludes universal filter ordering and absolute trailing-column or GIN-operator claims.

sources.title: Scale for high-volume workloads
sources.shortSummary: Documents actual CPU/memory/I/O driven vertical scaling, asynchronous read-only replicas with separate endpoints, primary routing for immediate reads and workload-dependent caching. Excludes fixed SKU ranges, universal thresholds, legacy Redis endpoints and discounts.

sources.title: Connection optimization
sources.shortSummary: Documents transaction/session/statement pooling, borrowed connection contexts, transaction-local settings, bounded retry and per-instance pool budgets. Does not rely on blanket session reset guarantees, prepared-statement incompatibility or dated tier connection limits.

sources.title: Client libraries and development best practices
sources.shortSummary: Documents OSS same-slot multi-key requirements, Enterprise command exceptions, cluster-capable clients, pipeline efficiency and SCAN rather than blocking KEYS. Does not use external Redis/GitHub links as technical citations.

sources.title: Implement data operations
sources.shortSummary: Documents Redis string/hash/list/counter operations, atomic numeric increments, cache-aside invalidation, key-level TTL/EXPIRE/PERSIST and incremental SCAN. SETEX is specifically string-only despite a broad introductory sentence.

sources.title: Index and query vector data
sources.shortSummary: Documents index key prefixes, HASH binary vectors, dimension/type matching, KNN dialect 2 and EF_RUNTIME. Excludes pipeline atomicity generalization, unsupported absolute model-metric assertions and unbounded range-result-count claims.

sources.title: Choose vector types and indexing strategies
sources.shortSummary: Documents FLOAT32/FLOAT64 element widths and workload-tested precision tradeoffs, FLAT/HNSW differences and query-local EF_RUNTIME. No universal memory-total, latency, recall or metric suitability guarantee is used.

sources.title: Optimize Redis data structures for vector storage
sources.shortSummary: Documents flat HASH field/binary-vector storage versus RedisJSON nested documents/numeric-array vectors with matching index types. Excludes migration that overwrites an existing HASH key with JSON without removal and claims about exact JSON memory size.

sources.title: Optimize performance when using pgvector in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
sources.shortSummary: Directly linked product reference distinguishes estimated versus measured EXPLAIN, fixed-dimension standard vector indexes, all-lists IVFFlat exact-search fallback, runtime versus build parameters and partial-index predicate matching. Excludes the SET-without-LOCAL transaction example and generalized modern alternative-type dimension limits.

sources.title: Explore Azure Service Bus concepts and messaging in AI architectures
sources.shortSummary: Broker queues absorb bursts and decouple request intake from processing. Standard and Premium have different capacity models. Queue allocation is not exactly-once processing; reliability claims use the separate receive-mode unit.

sources.title: Choose between queues and topics with subscriptions
sources.shortSummary: Queues allocate work among competing receivers; topic subscriptions receive independent copies. Sessions group ordered work. Subscription SQL, correlation and Boolean filters have different predicate capabilities and valid use cases.

sources.title: Structure messages for AI workloads
sources.shortSummary: Application properties carry routing metadata; message IDs support configured duplicate detection and correlation IDs track a request. Claim-check separates large data from broker messages, TTL bounds validity, and batches must retry the overflowing message in a new batch.

sources.title: Process messages reliably
sources.shortSummary: PeekLock and receive-and-delete trade settlement reliability for overhead. Complete, abandon, defer and dead-letter serve distinct outcomes. Delivery limits, explicit DLQ resubmission and lock renewal are documented; renewal does not guarantee exactly-once effects.

sources.title: Understand Azure Event Grid concepts and event-driven patterns for AI solutions
sources.shortSummary: Custom topics receive application events, system topics receive provider events, subscriptions define selection/destination, and handlers process deliveries. Candidates avoid namespace MQTT and unbounded latency assertions.

sources.title: Work with event schemas and properties
sources.shortSummary: CloudEvents fields distinguish origin, operation, identity and subject. Type, subject and typed-data filters can be combined. Custom-topic input and subscription output schemas have asymmetric compatibility.

sources.title: Configure delivery and retry policies for reliable event processing
sources.shortSummary: Traditional custom-topic webhook delivery uses acknowledgement, endpoint-specific error treatment, time and attempt limits, optional Blob dead-letter storage and all-or-none batches. Selected claims exclude the introductory overgeneralization that every unsuccessful status retries.

sources.title: Publish custom events from AI applications
sources.shortSummary: Applications create custom topics and publish CloudEvents with SDK or REST. Managed-identity publication requires EventGrid Data Sender; events describe checkpoints and reference detailed outputs. No GitHub SDK link is admitted.

sources.title: Understand Azure Functions hosting and scaling for AI workloads
sources.shortSummary: Hosting and initialization affect cold-start latency; function execution timeout differs from the HTTP response limit. Async intake can hand work to Service Bus. Candidates avoid absolute Premium cold-start promises and blanket unbounded-execution assertions.

sources.title: Set up the local development environment for Functions
sources.shortSummary: Core Tools hosts local triggers; function_app.py, host.json, requirements.txt and .funcignore have separate roles. Azurite supplies local host storage. Deployment/settings commands must preserve production configuration. The Python reference resolves the unit’s overbroad publish-with-settings wording.

sources.title: Create triggers and bindings for AI integration patterns
sources.shortSummary: Python v2 uses decorators, one trigger and optional input/output bindings. Service Bus triggers and output parameters integrate queued work with storage. Reusing explicit SDK clients avoids per-invocation initialization. Preview SDK-type extensions are not used.

sources.title: Manage secrets and configuration in Functions
sources.shortSummary: Local settings are separate from hosted app configuration. Fetching remote settings and local machine encryption support development workflows. Questions do not make immediate refresh claims about centralized configuration or secret references.

sources.title: Configure identity and access for Functions
sources.shortSummary: Named Service Bus identity connections pair a fullyQualifiedNamespace prefix with Receiver or Sender roles. Function/host/admin keys have separate scopes and do not identify callers. Host storage remains a separate dependency.

sources.title: Azure Functions developer reference guide for Python apps
sources.shortSummary: Python v2 route_params reads route segments; blueprints must be registered with the main app. requirements.txt drives remote dependencies, .funcignore excludes deployment files, and changing Python version requires rebuilding and redeploying artifacts. Preview or new worker-version controls are excluded.

sources.title: Azure Functions triggers and bindings
sources.shortSummary: Exactly one trigger invokes a function; optional input/output directions differ by binding. The 4.x table distinguishes Blob/Cosmos standalone input support from Service Bus/Event Grid trigger and output support. Python ServiceBusReceivedMessage SDK-type trigger is Preview and is not used.

sources.title: CloudEvents v1.0 schema with Azure Event Grid
sources.shortSummary: The explicit compatibility table permits CloudEvents-to-CloudEvents and both Event Grid input output formats, but not CloudEvents input to Event Grid output. Candidate claims do not use the article’s old Functions runtime samples.

sources.title: Understand event filtering for Event Grid subscriptions
sources.shortSummary: Concrete subject boundaries, scalar predicate types, AND across filters, OR within values, and missing-key behavior support exact routing evaluations. Scalar data paths avoid the article’s inconsistent CloudEvents top-level key descriptions.

sources.title: Authentication and authorization with Microsoft Entra ID
sources.shortSummary: Publishing authorization requires events/send/action, provided by EventGrid Data Sender. A resource, resource-group or subscription assignment has different scope. Token acquisition alone is not authorization; disableLocalAuth API examples are excluded.

sources.title: Azure Functions developer guide
sources.shortSummary: A function app is the deployment/runtime-management boundary, whereas projects and blueprints organize code. Publishing targets an existing app; host storage and SDK clients are separate connection responsibilities.

sources.title: Store and organize secrets, keys, and certificates
sources.shortSummary: Supports secret/key/certificate purpose, exact secret RBAC roles, metadata visibility, vault boundaries and soft-delete recovery. Excludes the unit’s broad HSM/key-export/key-type generalizations; no claim that all secrets use HSM protection.

sources.title: Retrieve secrets using Azure SDK client libraries
sources.shortSummary: Supports SecretClient value versus metadata reads, error categories, async client/credential lifetimes and reuse. Do not treat its abbreviated DefaultAzureCredential list as a complete version-independent chain. Linked Python API readme is captured separately but unapproved.

sources.title: Handle secret versioning and rotation
sources.shortSummary: Supports creation of new versions, metadata inspection, disabling a specific version, informational expiry, rotation patterns and explicit consumer refresh. Excludes latest-enabled fallback and deletion of individual historical versions; no automatic secret rotation policy claim.

sources.title: Implement caching strategies to reduce Key Vault calls
sources.shortSummary: Supports per-process TTL, startup preload, distributed-cache tradeoffs, monotonic elapsed-time measurement, event invalidation with TTL fallback and jittered retry. Use separately retrieved service limits for exact quotas; cache design bounds require successful refresh and stated concurrency.

sources.title: Connect to App Configuration from application code
sources.shortSummary: Supports Python provider Mapping, JSON content type, literal keys, SettingSelector order, trimming, managed-identity data roles and explicit refresh calls gated by an interval. No quickstart ancestry inferred from the generic provider name.

sources.title: Organize settings with labels and feature flags
sources.shortSummary: Supports key-label identity, null-label defaults, ordered composition and separately enabled feature-flag refresh plus FeatureManager evaluation. A sentinel is a publication signal, not a transaction or a wall-clock scheduler.

sources.title: Reference Key Vault secrets from App Configuration
sources.shortSummary: Supports reference content type, actual client-side secret resolution, independently scoped data roles, keyvault_credential and secret_refresh_interval. Excludes HSM-for-all-secrets, automatic secret rotation-policy and unconditional refresh assertions.

sources.title: Decide what to store in App Configuration vs Key Vault
sources.shortSummary: Supports sensitivity-based placement and reference indirection only. Rejects the unit’s generalized HSM and expiry-enforcement claims; no unsupported lifecycle/security comparison is carried into questions.

sources.title: Explore OpenTelemetry and its role in observability
sources.shortSummary: Text tab establishes APIs, SDKs, instrumentation, exporters, trace/span/parent identity and W3C HTTP context. Supports semantic mappings without using video, assessments or release-status inference.

sources.title: Add the OpenTelemetry SDK to an application
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports Python Distro startup, explicit code connection precedence, service namespace/name and instance identity. Python version prerequisite is taken from the direct current product page; automatic logging and instrumentation are not generalized to every library.

sources.title: Configure spans and traces
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports span kinds, resource-versus-span attributes, context-manager lifetime, handled exception recording and explicit error status. Generic nested-span latency question is withheld as an installed AI-103 duplicate.

sources.title: Export telemetry to Azure Monitor
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports export tables, Python sampling overrides, independent metric signal and bounded offline retry. Current product page supplies 1.8.6 default boundary. Multiple services appearing in Logs is not treated as proof of context propagation.

sources.title: Debug distributed flows with trace data
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports trace waterfall, emitter identity, operation_Id correlation and KQL customDimensions conversion. Joining on operation_Id establishes trace membership rather than immediate parentage or causal proof.

sources.title: Write basic KQL queries
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports Application Insights versus workspace table names, pipe/where/project/extend semantics, aggregates, distinct estimates and chart presentation. Binning-only question is excluded as an installed SC-200 duplicate.

sources.title: Explore logs for errors and performance
sources.shortSummary: Text tab supports itemCount-weighted estimates, explicit inner joins, column disambiguation and per-target latency aggregation. Correct the example’s mislabeled request-role/exception-emitter interpretation; never promise exact reconstruction from sampling.

sources.title: Enable Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for .NET, Node.js, Python, and Java applications
sources.shortSummary: Current direct product page supports Python 3.10+, Azure Monitor Distro initialization and destination setup. Release-status section delegates detailed maturity to a FAQ not directly linked by training; it does not assert every feature GA.

sources.title: Configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry
sources.shortSummary: Current product page supports Python resource identity, sampling types/units, 1.8.6 default, trace-based log filtering and storage override. Live Metrics carries an explicit Python Preview legal notice; no Java-only overrides, native ingestion or GenAI extensions are borrowed.

sources.title: Add and modify Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for .NET, Java, Node.js, and Python applications
sources.shortSummary: Read Python custom telemetry and exception sections: automatic escaping exceptions, manual record_exception, and language-specific customization. Community experimental instrumentations and GenAI feedback extensions are excluded.

sources.title: Log queries in Azure Monitor
sources.shortSummary: Current article grounds Azure Monitor KQL/log-query use and explicitly distinguishes supported scope from Azure Data Explorer-only constructs. Linked operator references are not silently admitted through a doc-to-doc chain.

sources.title: Azure Key Vault service limits
sources.shortSummary: Current vault-resource quotas: 4,000 other transactions and collective 300 CREATE secret/IMPORT certificate/IMPORT key per 10 seconds; subscription limit five times per vault. Backup bound 500 versions, no individual-version deletion, same-subscription/geography restoration. Managed HSM has separate limits.
